core.title: Give every train exactly one route or a typed single-route assessment
core.given: The plan's registered trains and the routes of all registered interlockings.
core.when: The plan reaches CONFIRM (every registered train is checked, whatever changed).
core.then: Make each registered train exactly one of: route-targeted (selected by exactly one route across all registered interlockings) or typed single-route (declares the single-route classification with a basis from the closed vocabulary) — never both, never neither.
prefer: Route-targeted: exactly one route across all registered interlockings selects the train.
Typed single-route: the single-route classification plus a basis from the closed vocabulary.
avoid: No route and no classification, assuming that implies direct dispatch — an omission.
Declaring single-route on a route-targeted train — a contradiction.
Free prose as the single-route basis.
Treating a train selected by zero or several routes as route-targeted; only a count of exactly one qualifies.
core.why: Route-space was optional metadata, so a train with no route analysis looked like one whose analysis concluded single-route; silence read as proof analysis happened. Explicit classification surfaces the omission at planning time.
evidence: The admission check for this rule passes at the CONFIRM phase over all registered trains.
On failure, each offending train is reported with its identifier, plan location, selecting route ids, declared classification, basis and admission status (field names under core.verification).
verification: Scope: at the CONFIRM phase the check evaluates every registered train, not only those changed by the current diff; it is confirm-blocking — earlier phases are not gated, though the planner should already author compliant trains.
Severity 4; disposition strict: every finding fails the check; findings are not advisory.
route_targeted = the train is selected by exactly one route, counted across every registered interlocking; a count of 0 or of more than 1 is not route_targeted.

typed_single_route = the declared classification is single-route AND the basis is a member of the closed basis vocabulary; free prose does not qualify. Membership in the closed vocabulary is owned by the realization's plan schema and its checker, not by this core.
exactly_one: route_targeted XOR typed_single_route; both is a contradiction, neither is an omission.
On failure the report carries, for each offending train: train_id, train_path, route_ids, classification, basis, admission_status.

fires: At CONFIRM, a newly registered train is selected by no registered interlocking route and declares no typed single-route assessment.
At CONFIRM, a pre-existing registered train has neither route nor typed assessment, even though the current change touched no train or route.
A train is route-targeted (exactly one route) and also declares the single-route classification.
A train declares single-route with a free-prose basis instead of a closed-vocabulary basis.
An interlocking is unregistered or a route removed/retargeted, leaving a train with neither route nor typed assessment.
A train is selected by routes in two registered interlockings (count 2, so not route-targeted) and declares no typed single-route assessment.
doesNotFire: A train selected by exactly one route across all registered interlockings and declaring no single-route classification.
A train that is not route-targeted and declares the single-route classification with a closed-vocabulary basis.
Phases other than CONFIRM (the check is confirm-blocking; earlier phases are not gated, though the planner should already author compliant trains).

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact construct by which a train entry declares its route-space classification and the basis for it — the fields the admission check reads for the typed single-route assessment.
profileRequirements.bunValue: route_space.classification == single-route AND basis is a member of the closed vocabulary

proposedKeys.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact construct by which a train declares its route-space classification and basis — the stack's realization of the neutral 'typed single-route declaration' concept.
proposedKeys.bunValue: route_space.classification == single-route AND basis is a member of the closed vocabulary
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The urn group only covers URN shapes, declarations and bindings; no idiom key describes a plan artifact's internal route-space declaration fields, which vary with each stack's plan schema.

neutralityNotes: Plan-model terms (train, interlocking, route, registration, route-space classification, closed basis vocabulary) and the CONFIRM lifecycle phase are treated as method-level vocabulary shared by every realization, so they stay in the core; only the concrete declaration fields were pushed to the profile via the proposed key idiom.route_space_declaration. The members of the closed basis vocabulary are not enumerated in bun.json, so the core keeps the checker-owned deference in verification (like roots.excluded). Detector/validator/finding ids, and this realization's validator test ref, are bunOnly; per-rule severity (4) and strict disposition moved to core.verification as instructed. The '(issue #1554)' provenance reference was dropped from core avoid[0] (it survives in bun.json's audit) without changing the obligation.
